newsitem.title: USA: University sparks protest by dropping commentaries.
newsitem.headline: University sparks protest by dropping commentaries.

text.p: Temple University's decision to cancel a series of public radio commentaries from death row by black activist Mumia Abu-Jamal drew criticism Tuesday from the series producer and a journalists' organisation.
Julie Drizen, executive producer of Pacifica Radio's "Democracy Now" series, said the decision was "the most pernicious form of censorship."
"They made their decision based on fear of persecution," Drizen told Reuters.

It was the second journalistic controversy sparked by the commentaries of Abu-Jamal, a one-time Black Panther and radio journalist who has appealed his conviction and death sentence for the 1981 killing of a Philadelphia policeman.
National Public Radio dropped plans in 1994 to carry a series of Abu-Jamal commentaries on prison life after Philadelphia's police union and Republican U.S. Senate leader Bob Dole objected.
Abu-Jamal's case has drawn wide interest from foreign political leaders, death-penalty opponents and Hollywood activists.

Temple told Drizen Monday its radio station, WRTI-FM, was cancelling the series and another news programme from Pacifica, a Berkeley, California, public radio service that covers news of interest to left-wing listeners.
Drizen attributed the cancellation to a fear of losing state funding at the hands of Pennsylvania Gov. Tom Ridge, who signed Abu-Jamal's death warrant, which has since been stayed.
In a letter, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, Temple said it cancelled the broadcasts because of a shift in programming emphasis but it said the Abu-Jamal series hastened the move.

"Quite frankly, the decision was accelerated by news that 'Democracy Now' would air the Mumia Abu-Jamal radio commentaries," Temple public affairs director George Ingram said in the letter. He cited concerns about the appropriateness of airing commentary from a convicted murder seeking a new trial.
Ingram was unavailable for comment Tuesday, an aide said.
The Society of Professional Journalists said in a statement: "The sudden, abrupt decision to preempt Pacifica's 'Democracy Now' is clearly an act of censorship."

Peter Sussman, president of the organisation's Northern California chapter, said: "We can't make effective criminal justice policies without hearing all of the parties to various criminal justice disputes."

Drizen said the cancellation effectively silenced the Abu-Jamal broadcasts in his home state. "It (the series) ran on dozens of other stations across the country but not in the state of Pennsylvania, the state that's planning to execute this man."
